problem: Learned VLA skills that succeed from clean skill-boundary snapshots stall when chained, because a skill can meet its own postcondition yet leave a state (pose, objects, views) from which the next skill cannot start. Prior agent/TAMP/tool-API systems do not diagnose this semantic handoff failure.
motivation: Long-horizon household tasks need many composed language-conditioned skills, and agent-orchestrated VLA libraries promise broader coverage than symbolic APIs. Task success is near zero in BEHAVIOR-1K, so aggregate success gives no actionable signal about what the VLA skills must learn next.
key_idea: Use an agent harness (typed skill contracts, plan-act-verify-replan with a multi-view VLM verifier, replayable traces) to compare the same pi0.5 skill checkpoints from clean snapshots versus chained states and attribute failures to next-skill readiness, target grounding, and control execution.
insight: Skills are competent in isolation (77-100% from snapshots) yet task success is near zero, so the bottleneck is the chained-state distribution shift between composed policies, not weak per-skill policies. The arm-reach verifier ablation (only the navigation criterion changes) surfaces 12 more readiness failures, triggers 25 more move_to attempts and recovers the radio task, while control/commit failures remain dominant.
method: Semantic skill contract: each call s_t=(name,args,prompt,budget B_s,verifier interval K_s,postcondition phi_t) over 9 skills (move_to, pick_up_from, place_on, place_in, press, open_door, ...).

pi0.5 skill library: PaliGemma 2B + 300M flow-matching action expert over head + two wrist RGB views and proprioception; 50k-step all-skill mid-training then skill-group post-training (nav, switch/press, door, grasp, surface placement, containment placement).

Plan-act-verify-replan loop: execute a VLA chunk for K=200 steps, query gemini-2.5-flash on head/wrist views; advance on positive verdict with confidence >0.6 ('uncertain' never terminates), else continue, retry or replan within per-skill and episode budgets.

Handoff-aware postcondition: move_to postcondition requires the target close-up at arm-reach distance, approximating next-skill readiness; a formal rho(s_t,s_{t+1}) template library is proposed as future work.

Trace-based failure attribution: replayable traces parsed into per-skill attempts, classified from structured verifier reasons into control execution, target grounding, and next-skill readiness, with a blinded human audit of verifier failure decisions.
Two-protocol evaluation: isolated snapshot single-skill benchmark vs. chained end-to-end rollouts using the same checkpoints and instances.

setting.backbone: pi0.5 (PaliGemma 2B + 300M action expert, fine-tuned) as skills; gemini-2.5-flash (frozen) as verifier
setting.training_data: Cleaned BEHAVIOR-1K teleoperation demonstrations segmented into skills; per task 180 train / 20 val episodes; 50k-step mid-training + 60k-200k step skill-group post-training
setting.observation: three 224x224 RGB views (head + two wrists) plus proprioception
setting.action_space: multi-step continuous action chunks from a flow-matching action expert (BEHAVIOR-1K robot)
setting.privileged: none at test time for the policy (final task success scored via BDDL predicate; progress scored by human video inspection)

numbers.eval_set_note: validation-split demonstration-segment snapshots from the same instances evaluated end-to-end; small per-skill samples
numbers.extra: VLM-verifier success with human review, not BDDL predicate

numbers.extra: K=200 steps; global budget 2x human demo length; progress score is human-scored fraction of the reference plan

numbers.eval_set_note: one representative round, one instance per task

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; BEHAVIOR-1K skill/task diagnostics only. Small n (n=3 rounds; single representative round for failure counts).
results: Isolated skills reach 77-100% success from snapshots (e.g. pick_up_from 28/29, open_door 7/7), yet end-to-end task success is near zero (1/10 tasks solved under the arm-reach criterion, 0/10 with reached-area) and mean progress is 19.5%. Of 130 failed attempts, 37 are target grounding, 35 next-skill readiness, and 58 control (31 grasp, 15 actuation, 12 placement); a blinded audit judged 20/21 verifier failures real.
limitations: Small pilot: few rollouts, n=3 progress, and one representative round for attribution; counts are not population-level.
Failure categories are derived from VLM verifier reasons, and the human audit validates only the binary failure decision on a small set; progress is scored by a single annotator.
Formal next-skill readiness predicate, no-recovery ablation, and verifier-cadence sweep are not evaluated; only simulation with under-specified object binding.
